name: Giuoco Piano — Tactics
description: 4 tactical challenges for White in the Italian Game. Find the winning 2-move sequence!

drills.name: The d5 Knight Overload
drills.description: White pressures the knight on d5 with Rfe1, then piles up with Ne4.
drills.briefExplanation: White pins the knight on d5 and prepares to overload it with multiple attackers.
drills.explanation: Ne4 brings the second knight into the attack. White follows with Nf4 (adding a third attacker) and Nxd5, overloading the defender. Black usually loses material or is forced to create a strong passed d-pawn for White.

drills.name: The f7 Assault
drills.description: White launches a direct attack on the vulnerable f7-pawn with Ng5.
drills.briefExplanation: White launches a direct attack on the weak f7-pawn, supported by the bishop on c4 and queen on b3.
drills.explanation: Nxf7! is the winning blow. The knight forks the rook on h8 and attacks the queen while exposing Black's king. If Black recaptures with Rxf7, White plays Qxf7+ and wins decisive material. If Kxf7 instead, Qxf7+ launches a mating attack. Black's position collapses.

drills.name: Ne5 Central Outpost
drills.description: White plants a powerful knight in the center attacking c6 and f7.
drills.briefExplanation: White plants a powerful knight in the center, attacking both c6 and f7 at once.
drills.explanation: If Black defends with c6, White captures on c6. After dxe5 (opening the d-file) and Re1 or Qxb7, White gains a strong initiative and often wins a pawn while Black's pieces remain uncoordinated.

drills.name: Qb3 + Bc4 Battery
drills.description: White maximizes the deadly battery already aimed at f7 with Rfe1 and Ng5.
drills.briefExplanation: The Qb3+Bc4 battery is already aimed at f7. Rfe1 loads the rook onto the e-file, preparing the decisive breakthrough.
drills.explanation: Ng5 adds the knight to create overwhelming pressure on f7. White follows with Nxf7 ideas and Rxf7, creating pressure on f7 that is very difficult for Black to defend without making further weaknesses.
